domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
m is an integer and 0 <= m <= n - 1
summation index k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n
division by k is valid because k is at least 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 1, define H_n = sum from k = 1 to n of 1/k and define g_n(m) = m minus sum from k = 1 to n of floor((k*m)/n) divided by k. Then g_n(m) <= H_n - 1. Moreover, g_n(m) = H_n - 1 holds if and only if m = n - 1.
quantifier_order: for all n in integers with n greater than 1
for all m in integers with 0 less than or equal to m and m less than or equal to n minus 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: outer parameter; defines the index range of sums and the harmonic-like quantity H_n

variables.name: m
variables.role: input to g_n(m); restricted to the integer interval 0 <= m <= n-1

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index running from 1 to n

variables.domain: values of the finite sum of real numbers 1/k for k from 1 to n
variables.name: H_n

variables.domain: values of m minus sum_{k=1}^n floor((k*m)/n) divided by k (as a real/rational expression)
variables.name: g_n(m)
variables.role: defined expression involving floor((k*m)/n) and division by k

variables.name: floor
variables.role: integer-valued floor function applied to the rational number (k*m)/n

witness_dependencies: no existential quantifiers are present; the equality characterization is explicit: g_n(m) equals H_n minus 1 exactly when m equals n minus 1

statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, if g_n(m) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor((k*m)/n)/k and H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, then g_n(m) <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if m = n - 1.
